data.title: Rejected-before reads the alternative's name, puts a title's 'not X' on X's side, and weighs the choice by its title
data.why: Measured 2026-10-12 on the KAD-61 set, now a test: the rule had drifted to 4 of 10 named and 3 false alarms on this journal, and was silent on a journal one day old — the first thing onboarding shows. The reason after the colon matched ordinary work ('fix the failing test'); the topic sat on both sides; a title like 'Postgres, not MongoDB' counted the alternative as chosen; the why argued with the alternative in its own words. The new rule names 9 of 10 with no false alarm, and catches the fresh-journal case.
data.rejected: Comparing only the words exclusive to each side: on a large journal the alternative's words are common and left almost nothing (DEC-26 at 0.07); Lowering REJECTED_SHARE: more names, but the false alarms came from reason words, not from the threshold
